title: Particle Physics Driven by Quantum Technology - Quantum Simulations and Quantum Sensing
authors: Itay M. Bloch, Marcela Carena, Yifan Chen, Xinran Li, Ying-Ying Li, Jing Shu
abstract: We review recent advances in particle physics enabled and motivated by the rapid progress of quantum technologies. The continued development of quantum computing toward large-scale, fault-tolerant systems has the potential to address dynamical problems that remain extremely challenging for classical computational approaches, opening new avenues for studying nonperturbative dynamical processes. Tabletop detectors and quantum-enhanced technologies have reached unprecedented sensitivities, enabling novel searches for ultralight particles, gravitational waves, and other physics beyond the Standard Model in parameter regimes previously inaccessible to conventional instrumentation. Taken together, these developments highlight a rapidly evolving landscape in which quantum technologies are beginning to reshape fundamental physics. We aim to synthesize recent progress and illuminate the opportunities they present for advancing particle physics in the coming years.
summary: This review surveys how rapid progress in quantum technologies—specifically quantum simulation and quantum sensing—is poised to revolutionize particle physics. It highlights that quantum computers can tackle classically intractable problems in Quantum Field Theory, while ultra-sensitive detectors can search for elusive physics beyond the Standard Model. Ultimately, the paper argues that quantum tools are reshaping the frontier of fundamental physics research.
main_problem: The paper addresses how emerging quantum technologies can be leveraged to tackle fundamental, classically intractable problems in particle physics, particularly those beyond the Standard Model.
main_result: Quantum computing and quantum sensing are emerging as uniquely powerful platforms capable of simulating non-perturbative Quantum Field Theory dynamics and achieving unprecedented sensitivity for detecting weak physical signals.
method: The review synthesizes progress across two main avenues: quantum simulation for QFT dynamics and quantum sensing for BSM searches, detailing the underlying quantum mechanical principles and technological requirements.
model_or_system: The scope covers diverse physical systems, including superconducting circuits (transmons, resonators), detectors (SNSPDs, KIDs), and theoretical models like Quantum Field Theories (QFT) for phenomena such as hadronization and dark matter interactions.
key_observables: Detection of faint BSM signals (e.g., axions), non-perturbative QFT dynamics, and measurements related to gravitational waves.
important_parameters: The required development towards large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum systems, and the sensitivity limits set by quantum noise sources.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that quantum technologies will mature sufficiently to overcome current computational and noise limitations to advance fundamental physics.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the direct connection between quantum sensing (using superconducting cavities/detectors for dark matter/GWs) and quantum simulation (using transmon processors for non-perturbative QFT dynamics).
paper_structure: The paper is structured as a review, first establishing the general motivation, then detailing the potential of quantum simulation for QFT, and subsequently covering the advancements in quantum sensing for BSM physics.
why_interesting: It provides a high-level roadmap connecting cutting-edge quantum hardware development (superconducting circuits, quantum algorithms) directly to fundamental physics questions, which is highly relevant for theorists working on open quantum systems and many-body dynamics.
